subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marine biologists study ocean ecosystems and organisms.
• They often conduct fieldwork in coastal and deep-sea environments.
• Silent Spring (1962) was written by Rachel Carson.
• Rachel Carson was a marine biologist before becoming a full-time writer.
prompt: The student wants to provide an example of a book Rachel Carson wrote. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Marine biologist Rachel Carson later became a full-time writer.
choices.B: The 1962 book Silent Spring is one example of Rachel Carson's work as a writer.
choices.C: In marine biology, researchers study ocean ecosystems and the organisms that live in coastal and deep-sea environments.
choices.D: As a marine biologist, Rachel Carson conducted research before transitioning to a career as a writer.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it directly accomplishes the stated rhetorical goal by providing a specific example of a book Rachel Carson wrote. The sentence names Silent Spring, includes its publication year (1962), and explicitly frames it as 'one example of Rachel Carson's work as a writer.' This choice draws on relevant information from the notes (specifically the third note) and presents it in a way that clearly fulfills the task of exemplifying Carson's written work.
